questions.questionText: Arrange the following tribal and peasant uprisings in chronological order: (i) Santhal Uprising (ii) Deccan Riots (iii) Munda Ulgulan (iv) Moplah Revolts. Choose the correct code:
questions.explanation: Chronology: Santhal Uprising (1855-1856), Deccan Agrarian Riots (1875), Birsa Munda's Ulgulan (1899-1900), and the Moplah Revolts of Malabar (culminating in 1921).

questions.questionText: The Muslim peasants of Malabar in Kerala who revolted against British authorities and Jenmi landlords in 1921 were known as:
questions.explanation: The Muslim peasants of Malabar were known as Moplahs (or Mappilas). The 1921 Moplah Rebellion was an armed uprising against both British colonial authorities and oppressive feudal Jenmi landlords.

questions.questionText:
Match List-I (Foreign Travelers) with List-II (Indian Rulers / Patrons):
List-I:
(A) Ibn Battuta
(B) Nicolo Conti
(C) Abdur Razzaq
(D) Domingo Paes
List-II:
1. Mohd. Bin Tughlaq
2. Devaraya I
3. Devaraya II
4. Krishnadevaraya
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta (from Morocco) visited Delhi during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and was appointed Qazi. Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara under Devaraya I, Abdur Razzaq under Devaraya II, and Domingo Paes under Krishnadevaraya.

questions.questionText: Which among the following foreign travelers arrived from Tangier (Morocco) and was appointed Qazi of Delhi for over six years under Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta arrived in India in 1334 during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who appointed him the Qazi of Delhi. His travelogue 'Kitab-ur-Rihla' provides vivid contemporary accounts of Tughlaq's court.

questions.questionText: Consider the names of the following Mughal Emperors of the Eighteenth century: (i) Alamgir II (ii) Ahmad Shah (iii) Jahandar Shah (iv) Muhammad Shah. Which among the following sequences represents the correct chronological order?
questions.explanation: Chronology of 18th-century later Mughal emperors: (iii) Jahandar Shah (1712-1713) -> (iv) Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela' (1719-1748) -> (ii) Ahmad Shah Bahadur (1748-1754) -> (i) Alamgir II (1754-1759).

questions.questionText:
Match List-I (Wars / Treaties) with List-II (Associated Events):
List-I:
(A) First Anglo-Maratha War
(B) Second Anglo-Maratha War
(C) Third Anglo-Maratha War
(D) Treaty of Salbai
List-II:
1. Treaty of Bassein
2. Warren Hastings
3. Lord Hastings & Abolition of Peshwa
4. Treaty of Purandhar
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Bassein (1802) signed by Peshwa Baji Rao II with the British led directly to the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-1805), as Scindia and Bhonsle refused to accept British subsidiary alliance.

questions.questionText: The Treaty of Bassien (1802) was signed between:
questions.optionA: The English and Peshwa Baji Rao II
questions.optionB: The English and Daulat Rao Sindhia
questions.optionC: The English and Jaswant Rao Holkar
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Bassein was signed on 31 December 1802 between the British East India Company (Lord Wellesley) and Maratha Peshwa Baji Rao II after the Peshwa was defeated by Holkar at the Battle of Poona.

questions.questionText: Arrange the following administrative and military measures of Akbar's reign in chronological order: (i) Introduction of Dagh system (ii) Introduction of Mansabdari system (iii) Promulgation of Mahzar (iv) Introduction of Dahsala system. Select the correct code:
questions.explanation: Chronology of Akbar's reforms: Introduction of Dagh (horse branding) in 1573-74, Mansabdari system formalization in 1574-75, Mahzar infallibility decree in 1579, and the Dahsala revenue system in 1580.
